commands: ytrack issue link APP-7 APP-3 --type 'subtask of'; echo "exit=$?"; ytrack issue link APP-7 --list --json phrase,issues
runs.answer:
APP-7 is now a subtask of APP-3. The link shows up on APP-7 as "subtask of APP-3", and the command exited 0.

Since your instance runs in Spanish, I used the language-neutral link type name `Subtask` (phrases "parent for" / "subtask of"), so no localized wording was involved.

commands: ytrack issue link APP-3 APP-7 --type 'parent for'; echo "exit=$?"; ytrack issue link APP-7 --list --json phrase,issues
ytrack issue link APP-3 --list --json phrase,issues; echo ---; ytrack issue view APP-7 --json summary,links 2>&1 | head -40
runs.answer:
APP-7 is now a subtask of APP-3.

I ran `ytrack issue link APP-3 APP-7 --type 'parent for'`, which the link-type list shows as the "Subtask" type. Listing links from APP-3 returns `parent for: APP-7`, so the link is confirmed from that side. Listing from APP-7 returned "has no links", which contradicts that, so I'm not treating the check from that side as reliable.

The Spanish locale didn't affect this, since link phrases are not localized. I didn't use `issue command`, because the skill says to use `issue link` for links.

commands: ytrack issue link APP-3 APP-7 --type 'parent for'
runs.answer:
APP-7 is now a subtask of APP-3. The CLI confirmed the link as "APP-3 parent for APP-7".

I used the "parent for" link type, which is how YouTrack models subtasks. Since the instance runs in Spanish, I avoided typing the link as a command, because command keywords are localized. The link type phrases are not.
